10.1002_smll.202510423: Proton‐conducting ceramic cells (PCCs) with BaCeO 3 ‐based electrolytes have emerged as promising energy conversion devices for low/intermediate‐temperature applications, and their performance critically depends on the microstructure of the composite hydrogen electrodes. However, the atomic‐level characterization and understanding of the interfacial interactions within the hydrogen electrode are still lacking. Herein, the atomic‐scale investigation of the high‐temperature element diffusion behavior and interface evolution between NiO and BaZr 0.1 Ce 0.7 Y 0.2 O 3‐δ （BZCY）is presented. The interdiffusion of Ni and Ba elements at the NiO/BZCY interface leads to the formation of a BaNiO x phase, and the interdiffusion extent is intensified with increasing the sintering temperature and time. The formation of BaNiO x , along with Ba loss‐induced stoichiometric deviation and Y 2 O 3 precipitation, impairs proton conduction in the hydrogen electrode and across the electrode/electrolyte interface. The results highlight the significance of atomic‐level interface modulation of the cermet hydrogen electrode, and a low‐temperature fabrication process is vital to improving the cell performance.
10.1002_smll.75836: Lithium oxalate (Li 2 C 2 O 4 ) attracts increasing attention as a cathode sacrificial prelithiation agent due to its high theoretical capacity, excellent air stability, residue‐free decomposition, and good compatibility with present battery chemistry. However, the sluggish decomposition kinetics of crystalline Li 2 C 2 O 4 results in a high decomposition potential. Herein, the interfacial decomposition behavior of crystalline Li 2 C 2 O 4 is systematically investigated. Theoretical calculations reveal that the NiCo 2 O 4 Li 2 C 2 O 4 interface substantially lowers the relative energies of key defect‐containing intermediates and reduces the energetic penalty for the rate‐determining Li + extraction step. Guided by this mechanism, a composite NiCo 2 O 4 @Li 2 C 2 O 4 prelithiation agent (NCO@LCO) is prepared by a facile freeze‐drying strategy. Benefiting from abundant catalytic interfaces, NCO@LCO exhibits accelerated decomposition kinetics, with the decomposition potential reduced from 4.45 to 4.24 V. When applied to a LiFePO 4 cathode through a secondary coating process and paired with a Si/C‐Gr anode, NCO@LCO provides additional active lithium during the first charge, increases the first‐cycle reversible capacity, and markedly improves long‐term cycling stability. This work provides a crystal‐interface perspective for Li 2 C 2 O 4 decomposition and demonstrates an efficient cathode‐side prelithiation strategy for improving the lithium inventory and cycling durability of silicon‐based lithium‐ion batteries.
10.1016_j.conbuildmat.2026.147963: The mechanism and consequences of passivation and chloride-induced corrosion initiation of steel in systems with reduced sulfur species (HS − , S n 2− , S 2 O 3 2− , SO 3 2− ), including reinforcement corrosion in concrete, are insufficiently understood to date. In this context, the present study investigated the electrochemical behaviour of carbon steel in synthetic pore solutions simulating ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBFS)-containing concrete, with a focus on the combined effects of reduced sulfur species and chloride, under anoxic, oxic and fully oxidised conditions. A three-electrode cell configuration was employed to conduct electrochemical analyses, including measurements of open-circuit potential (OCP), polarisation resistance ( R p ), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) to monitor passive film formation and stability. The critical chloride threshold ( c crit ) for steel corrosion initiation was studied by incremental NaCl additions to the synthetic pore solutions; these solution-based values serve as upper-bound estimates for steel embedded in concrete. In sulfide-containing solutions, steel did not passivate before complete oxidation of the reduced sulfur species, exhibiting OCP values of −550 to −700 mV Ag/AgCl and R p values of 3–50 kΩ·cm 2 . No corrosion initiation occurred up to 4 M chloride in solutions containing ≥ 50 mM HS − , even after oxygen exposure. The behaviour remained independent of pH because reduced sulfur species maintained anoxic conditions at the steel surface, with dissolved oxygen below the detection limit after days of air exposure. Passivation occurred only after complete oxidation of reduced sulfur species to sulfate, with R p increasing to 65–145 kΩ·cm². The effect of reduced sulfur species is therefore transient and ends when the oxidation front reaches the reinforcement and oxidises all reduced sulfur species, a process that may take decades in some cases of GGBFS concretes, during which conventional corrosion criteria and the critical chloride threshold concept are not applicable to these systems.
10.1016_j.est.2026.122076: This study investigates commercially available rechargeable batteries for long-term energy storage in low-power applications rated for low self-discharge rates. Through systematic evaluation under performance criteria relevant for such low-power systems, four promising candidates were selected for a detailed comprehensive characterization: a Nickel-Metal Hydride Low Self-Discharge (NiMH LSD) battery, a Sodium-ion (Na-ion) battery, a Lithium-ion battery with Lithium Titanium Oxide (LTO) anode, and a Lithium-ion battery with Iron Phosphate (LFP) cathode. A standardized testing methodology was developed to evaluate performance of these batteries under identical conditions at 25 °C, incorporating Capacity and Cycling performance assessment at multiple charging rates, Self-discharge measurement, and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy at various States of Charge. Results revealed distinctive performance profiles for each battery system. NiMH LSD demonstrated exceptional low self-discharge (~0% capacity loss over two months) with moderate energy conversion efficiency (89–91%), representing the ratio of energy recovered during discharge to energy input during charging. LTO-based Lithium-ion battery showed the expected superior cycling stability with minimal degradation and excellent coulomb efficiency (>99.5%) alongside with the lowest and most stable internal resistance. LFP-based Lithium-ion battery offered a balanced performance profile with good efficiency, a stable discharge voltage plateau between 3.2 and 3.3 V, and a moderate self-discharge (1.06%/month). Na-ion battery only showed good performance within the 20–80% SOC range with a linear voltage profile, but higher self-discharge (1.95%/month). Electrochemical impedance analysis identified unique resistance characteristics explaining these performance differences. This research demonstrates that battery selection for low-power applications should prioritize application-specific performance characteristics over general performance indicators such as energy density or standardized charge/discharge protocols. For backup-power systems requiring long-term energy storage with minimal maintenance, NiMH LSD proves optimal, while applications demanding exceptional cycle life would benefit from LTO-based Lithium-ion technology.
10.1021_acsami.5c16975: The development of intelligent, environmentally responsive oil–water separation membranes with reversible wettability presents a promising strategy for controllable emulsion separation and the advanced treatment of complex oily wastewater. Wastewater. In this study, a novel thermally responsive membrane with switchable wettability between superhydrophilic and superhydrophobic states was fabricated via in situ growth of bimetallic metal–organic frameworks (CoZn-ZIF) on electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride)/poly( N -isopropylacrylamide) (PVDF/PNIPAM) nanofiber membranes. The resulting PVDF/PNIPAM@CoZn-ZIF membrane leverages the thermally induced reversible conformational transition of PNIPAM to exhibit underwater superoleophobicity below its lower critical solution temperature (LCST) and under-oil superhydrophobicity above LCST. This switchable wettability enabled efficient on-demand separation of both oil-in-water (O/W) and water-in-oil (W/O) emulsions, achieving water permeation fluxes exceeding 1900 L·m –2 ·h –1 and oil permeation fluxes over 1150 L·m –2 ·h –1, with separation efficiencies above 99.00% and 99.60%, respectively. Moreover, the embedded Co 1 Zn 3 -ZIF served as a catalyst to activate peroxymonosulfate (PMS), generating reactive oxygen species ( · OH and · SO 4 – ) and enabling rapid degradation of methylene blue, with a removal efficiency of 99.92% within 15 min. This study presents a multifunctional composite membrane as an intelligent, efficient platform for integrated oil–water emulsion separation and organic pollutant remediation.
10.1021_acscatal.6c03848: The intrinsic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity can be effectively tailored by modifying the metal single-atom (SA) sites around atomic clusters (ACs). Here, strong interactions with single-atom Ce sites bind atomic Fe 4 clusters (Fe 4 ACs) containing Fe-O-Fe units onto Ce SA /N co-doped hollow carbon nanocage (Ce SA /HNC). The hollow nanocage-structured Ce SA /HNC with a large specific surface area, rich N-doped sites, and uniformly dispersed Ce single atoms can firmly anchor Fe 4 clusters to suppress aggregation. Owing to the strong synergism between Fe 4 AC active sites and a Ce SA electron regulator, Fe 4 -Ce SA /HNC delivers a high ORR half-wave potential of 0.931 V and a low OER overpotential of 326 mV at 10 mA cm −2, yielding an ultralow potential gap (Δ E ) of 0.619 V. Additionally, a liquid Zn-air battery based on this catalyst operates steadily for 1659 h. Experiment and theoretical calculations reveal that the Ce 4+ /Ce 3+ redox couple acts as an “electron pump” that stabilizes Fe against leaching via a cyclic electron transfer mechanism. Further mechanistic analysis demonstrates that the Fe 3d-O 2p orbital hybridization within the Fe-O-Fe units, together with the Fe 3d-Ce 4f orbital hybridization at the Fe 4 -Ce SA interface, jointly optimizes the adsorption strength of oxygen intermediates, thereby significantly boosting the ORR activity. This work advances highly effective energy-related electrocatalysis by providing a workable and feasible method for the accurate production of atomically distributed multi-metal core catalysts.
